title: Stolen 120-year-old bell recovered after vandalism at another church in Canada
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — Police have recovered a historic, century-old bell that was stolen from a Catholic church in rural Canada, but the vandals destroyed the bell tower. On November 14 near Fraserwood, Manitoba, police were notified that a 120-year-old bell at Sacred Heart of Jesus Church was stolen. Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) from Gimli came to investigate the November 14 theft and found that the church bell tower, which is about 1.5 stories tall, was heavily vandalized and the bell, which weighed around 300 pounds, was missing. The ornately decorated brass bell came from Switzerland in 1906. … Arsons against religious institutions have skyrocketed in the last few years. Federal data show that there were 592 reported arsons from 2010 to 2022. However, approximately 423 of these acts of violence were from 2015 onward. Conservative MPs have urged Liberal MPs for some time to back a bill that, if passed, would make church arsonists pay for the damages they cause as “vandalizing places of worship is unacceptable.” The Liberals thus far have refused to back the bill and recently blocked a motion that called for a study on church arsons in Canada.

title: Christian girl still missing in Pakistan after abduction, forced conversion
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — A 16-year-old girl remains missing in Pakistan weeks after she was allegedly abducted, converted to Islam, and forcibly married using falsified age documents. Samina, the daughter of Allah Ditta and Zarina Bibi, was reportedly taken by a local Muslim man named Muni and his associates while running an errand to buy milk on October 2 in Phoolnagar, an industrial and agricultural town in Punjab’s Kasur District where the struggling family lives. … According to data compiled by the Centre for Social Justice (CSJ), 515 cases of abduction and forced religious conversion of minority girls and women were documented across Pakistan between 2021 and 2025. The trend continued unabated in 2026, with CSJ recording at least 84 verified cases in the first 10 months of the year alone, 49 involving Christian victims and 35 involving Hindu victims. More than half of the documented victims in 2026 were confirmed minors under 18, including 37 ages 14 to 17 and six under age 14, underscoring how perpetrators routinely rely on fraudulent age declarations and marriage certificates while impoverished families face economic coercion and threats of violence when Until police enforce Punjab’s child marriage laws and hold perpetrators and complicit officials accountable, Samina’s family and countless other minority households remain trapped in fear without justice or protection.
